description: Site-specific failed approaches to avoid repeating

failed_approaches.approach: Using responsive PID allocation (pid_kp=0.001) to improve PFT#10 biomass
failed_approaches.why_failed: PID responds to light stress (dominant signal) rather than P stress when total productivity is extremely low, leading to maladaptive leaf allocation that worsens both leaf and root biomass
alternatives: Fix P starvation first before optimizing allocation strategy
Sequential targeted parameter modifications rather than allocation optimization

failed_approaches.approach: Applying SPSA optimization directly to underperforming PFTs without mechanistic diagnosis
failed_approaches.why_failed: SPSA assumes near local optimum but PFT#10 has mechanistic bottlenecks (zero P uptake, wrong turnover) that must be fixed first. Gradient-based optimization fails when applied to wrong parameter set
alternatives: Targeted parameter changes based on mechanistic understanding

failed_approaches.approach: Single-variable optimization (Method 1) focusing only on PFT#10 fineroot biomass
failed_approaches.why_failed: Achieved high PFT#10 fineroot (80% of target) by suppressing PFT#9 (93% underestimate) and causing massive AGB overshoot (13.7×)

failed_approaches.approach: mod5-7 parameter modification tests based on mod4 foundation with 90% MR reduction
failed_approaches.why_failed: mod4 foundation had ecosystem collapse from 90% maintenance respiration reduction, making all subsequent tests invalid

failed_approaches.approach: Equal weighting of all 9 outputs in composite NRMSE (Method 2)
failed_approaches.why_failed: Severely underestimates PFT#10 fineroot (9% of target) while achieving good shrub performance

failed_approaches.approach: Modifying cross-PFT parameters to help target PFT
failed_approaches.why_failed: Parameters that help one PFT harm others, creating optimization conflicts

failed_approaches.approach: Using shared phenology parameters for optimization
failed_approaches.why_failed: Shared parameters have opposite effects on different PFTs, cannot simultaneously optimize all
alternatives: Accept sub-optimal performance for some PFTs

failed_approaches.approach: Using simplified PyModel for phenology calibration
failed_approaches.why_failed: Missing cold status state machine logic - GDD accumulated continuously instead of conditionally, causing 31-day MAE vs 2.2-day MAE for full model
alternatives: Use full PyModel with complete state machine
Validate surrogate models thoroughly before calibration

failed_approaches.approach: Morris sampling with num_levels=8 for exponential phenology parameters
failed_approaches.why_failed: Grid resolution too coarse - optimal phen_c value fell between grid points, causing all 4,170 parameter combinations to miss optimal phenology
alternatives: Increase num_levels to 16 or 32 for sensitive parameters
Follow Morris screening with continuous optimization

failed_approaches.approach: Including 2000-2001 in phenology calibration
failed_approaches.why_failed: Initialization artifacts from nchilldays=0 startup caused wrong GDD threshold calculations in first two years
alternatives: Run 1999 spin-up to accumulate proper chilling days

failed_approaches.approach: Storage cushion hypothesis as primary bottleneck
failed_approaches.why_failed: Storage cushion creates targets but is irrelevant when NPP is negative - storage is being depleted, not filled. Absolute storage deficit is small (~0.3 g C/m²)
alternatives: Focus on making NPP positive first

failed_approaches.approach: PID controller root over-allocation as primary bottleneck
failed_approaches.why_failed: PID controller adjusts allocation of positive NPP only. When NPP is negative, PID is not active and allocation fractions become meaningless

failed_approaches.approach: Nitrogen limitation hypothesis
failed_approaches.why_failed: N supply (0.67 g N/m²) far exceeds demand (0.002 g N/m²) due to low stoich_nitr_leaf_10 (0.00122). N ratio >1000x sufficient

failed_approaches.approach: Further reduction of maintenance respiration via maintresp_nonleaf_baserate parameter
failed_approaches.why_failed: Parameter already at lower bound (1.296e-6 gC/gN/s), 49% below default, cannot be reduced further within Morris parameter space

failed_approaches.approach: Increasing photosynthetic capacity via leaf_slatop_10 parameter
failed_approaches.why_failed: Parameter at lower bound (0.00853 m²/gC), representing thickest possible leaves with minimum photosynthetic area per unit carbon, cannot increase GPP capacity further
alternatives: Expand upper SLA bounds to allow thinner leaves

failed_approaches.approach: Further phenology optimization via parameter adjustment
failed_approaches.why_failed: Phenology already optimized on Dec 7 with RMSE 4.2 days, Case #3643 parameters very close to optimal values, phenology timing is not the constraint
alternatives: Focus on carbon balance code modifications

failed_approaches.approach: Changing Arctic reference temperature from 20°C to 10°C
failed_approaches.why_failed: At spring temperature T=5°C, changing reference to 10°C increases MR scaling from 0.35 to 0.71, doubling MR and worsening carbon balance

failed_approaches.approach: Parameter optimization alone to solve spring carbon starvation
failed_approaches.why_failed: maintresp_nonleaf_baserate already at lower bound (1.296e-6, 49% below default) but still produces MR > GPP in spring

failed_approaches.approach: Reduce maintenance respiration by 90% to fix spring MR > GPP problem
failed_approaches.why_failed: Created ecosystem death spiral - GPP collapsed 58% while MR only reduced 85%, resulting in 52-56% less net carbon available

failed_approaches.approach: Increase storage cushion from collapsed baseline (mod4 foundation)
failed_approaches.why_failed: Extra carbon went to root over-allocation instead of leaves, making PFT#10 worse (-25% vs -13%)

failed_approaches.approach: Parameter tuning to achieve realistic Arctic graminoid biomass
failed_approaches.why_failed: Even best result (+58% improvement) still produced absolute biomass values too low for realistic Arctic ecosystem

failed_approaches.approach: Single replacement pattern for job file generation using 'PtCNPEn' only
failed_approaches.why_failed: Two different naming patterns exist: 'PtCNPEn' (no underscore) for script names and 'PtCNP_En' (with underscore) for parameter file paths
alternatives: Use chained replacements to handle both patterns
Verify all occurrences of replacement strings in different contexts

failed_approaches.approach: Assuming Morris parameter file has header row
failed_approaches.why_failed: Morris parameter file is pure data array (4170 rows × 138 columns) with NO HEADER, causing off-by-one indexing errors
alternatives: Always verify file structure before indexing

failed_approaches.approach: Universal phenology parameter application (mod_phen)
failed_approaches.why_failed: Phenology parameters calibrated from Case #561 caused 54% simulation failure rate and 91% performance regression when applied universally to all Morris parameter combinations
alternatives: Adaptive phenology parameters based on Morris parameter regime

failed_approaches.approach: Sequential modification strategy expecting universal improvement
failed_approaches.why_failed: The assumption that modifications would universally improve all cases was wrong - best Morris case (Set #2675) got worse with all modifications while best modified case (Set #2678) was only rank #7 in Morris
alternatives: Parameter space analysis to predict which cases benefit from modifications
Ensemble approach rather than single best parameter set

failed_approaches.approach: Using Case #561 phenology parameters for modifications
failed_approaches.why_failed: Caused 54% simulation failure rate (27/50 cases failed) because phenology was calibrated from a case not representative of successful parameter space
alternatives: Use phenology from best Morris case (Case #2675)
Calibrate phenology from representative successful cases
Use adaptive phenology calibration for different parameter regimes

failed_approaches.approach: Phenology-only modifications (phen2675)
failed_approaches.why_failed: Zero cases appeared in top 10 ranking, indicating phenology alone is insufficient for optimal performance

failed_approaches.approach: Single-objective optimization targeting only biomass
failed_approaches.why_failed: Creates systematic overestimation of MODIS LAI and GPP by 2-3× while achieving biomass targets

failed_approaches.approach: Using Case #561-based phenology modifications across all Morris cases
failed_approaches.why_failed: 54% failure rate because phenology was optimized for one parameter regime (low MR, low SLA) and incompatible with diverse Morris parameter combinations
alternatives: Use phenology from best Morris case (Case #2675)

failed_approaches.approach: Single-objective biomass optimization without ecosystem constraints
failed_approaches.why_failed: Creates 2-3x overestimation of ecosystem LAI and GPP, fails independent MODIS validation

failed_approaches.approach: Using optimized Case #2678 as baseline for realistic ecosystem modeling
failed_approaches.why_failed: Despite best biomass NRMSE, it systematically overestimates ecosystem fluxes and fails remote sensing validation
alternatives: Use Case #845 as baseline with PFT#9 specific modifications
Hybrid approach balancing biomass and ecosystem function

failed_approaches.approach: Single parameter optimization focusing only on biomass NRMSE
failed_approaches.why_failed: Creates unrealistic ecosystem function. Case #2678 matches biomass but overestimates MODIS LAI/GPP by 2-3×. Ignores ecosystem-level constraints.
alternatives: Constrained optimization with ecosystem function limits

failed_approaches.approach: Extreme storage cushion modification (4.4× increase to 3.0)
failed_approaches.why_failed: Even increasing alloc_storage_cushion_10 from 0.686 to 3.0 (well beyond Morris upper bound of 1.77) still underestimates PFT#10 biomass. Storage alone is insufficient.

failed_approaches.approach: Focusing on L:FR allocation ratios to fix biomass distribution
failed_approaches.why_failed: L:FR paradox shows allocation ratios don't determine absolute biomass. Total productivity is the bottleneck, not allocation fractions.

failed_approaches.approach: Attempting to fix Case #2678 with extreme parameter modifications
failed_approaches.why_failed: Even with extreme modifications (storage 4.4×, PID 430×), still fails PFT#10 biomass and causes 2-3× MODIS LAI/GPP overestimate due to structural growing season length issues

failed_approaches.approach: Using all 5 parameter modifications (Exp5) for complete fix
failed_approaches.why_failed: Seed supplement parameter causes 21-24% overshoot in LAI/GPP, degrading MODIS match despite improving PFT#9 biomass
alternatives: Use Exp3 or Exp4 (3-4 parameters only)

failed_approaches.approach: Modifying ecosystem-level phenology parameters (phen_coldtemp, phen_gddthresh_c)
failed_approaches.why_failed: Would affect all PFTs simultaneously and break the MODIS LAI/GPP match that is the main advantage of Case #845

failed_approaches.approach: Reading evaluation data from combined summary file
failed_approaches.why_failed: Summary file didn't contain the detailed biomass data needed for comprehensive evaluation
alternatives: Extract directly from MAT and NetCDF simulation files
Use original data sources with proper indexing

failed_approaches.approach: Using arithmetic mean for composite NRMSE calculation
failed_approaches.why_failed: Doesn't match the root mean square formula used in other scripts, causing inconsistent rankings

failed_approaches.approach: Extracting 845 experiment parameters from NetCDF files
failed_approaches.why_failed: NetCDF files only contain results, not the input parameters used for the simulation
alternatives: Start with Case #845 Morris parameters and apply documented modifications

failed_approaches.approach: Using separate parameter names like fates_stoich_nitr_leaf
failed_approaches.why_failed: FATES actually uses 2D arrays fates_stoich_nitr(organ, pft), not separate 1D parameters
alternatives: Use 2D parameter indexing with organ dimension

failed_approaches.approach: Using responsive PID allocation (pid_kp = 0.001) to improve PFT#10 biomass
failed_approaches.why_failed: PID responded to light stress (dominant signal) rather than P stress when total productivity was extremely low, causing maladaptive leaf allocation and biomass collapse
alternatives: Apply SPSA only after bottlenecks resolved

failed_approaches.approach: Applying SPSA optimization directly to allocation parameters
failed_approaches.why_failed: Cannot optimize allocation strategy until resource availability bottlenecks are fixed. SPSA assumes near local optimum but mechanistic bottlenecks (zero P uptake, wrong turnover) must be addressed first
alternatives: Correct turnover rate to literature values

failed_approaches.approach: Relying on Morris ensemble to identify all critical parameters
failed_approaches.why_failed: Morris ensemble missed fates_turnover_fnrt which caused 5× error in turnover rate and systematic 77% underestimation. P uptake parameters were included but all cases still showed zero P uptake
alternatives: Literature-based parameter priors for Arctic traits
Include all critical parameters in sensitivity analysis

failed_approaches.approach: Morris ensemble optimization with original parameter bounds
failed_approaches.why_failed: Parameter bounds were too restrictive for PFT#10, particularly for P uptake parameters that needed to be 10-100x higher than Morris upper bounds
alternatives: Expand P uptake parameter bounds by 10-100x
Test P uptake boost in Test 3

failed_approaches.approach: Boost PFT#10 P uptake parameters (vmax_p) by 10× to overcome P limitation
failed_approaches.why_failed: Triggered allocation paradox - higher vmax_p caused PID controller to reduce root allocation, decreasing total capacitance and worsening ECA competition performance

failed_approaches.approach: Single-PFT optimization for multi-PFT competitive system
failed_approaches.why_failed: Cannot solve zero-sum competition by optimizing one PFT in isolation when nutrients are limiting - competitive exclusion requires multi-PFT approach

failed_approaches.approach: Making up specific zi depth values as examples (0.0, 0.05, 0.15 meters) without verification
failed_approaches.why_failed: These were fabricated examples presented as facts, following same error pattern of making up values instead of verifying them from actual model configuration
alternatives: Describe mathematical relationships without specific values
Extract actual zi values from model configuration files
State when values are conceptual examples vs real data

failed_approaches.approach: Unbounded parameter optimization for root distribution calibration
failed_approaches.why_failed: Optimizer drove parameters to zero for graminoids, resulting in unrealistic uniform distributions

failed_approaches.approach: Weighted averaging across cores with irregular depth sampling for 'observed data' visualization
failed_approaches.why_failed: Created artificial data points that were not raw field measurements, smoothed out subsurface peaks, and distorted actual profile shapes

failed_approaches.approach: Fitting exponential formulas to individual graminoid cores with subsurface peaks
failed_approaches.why_failed: Mathematical impossibility - exponential formulas cannot represent subsurface peaks due to monotonic decrease constraint

failed_approaches.approach: Optimizing plant-side parameters (vmax_p, allocation, turnover) to solve P limitation
failed_approaches.why_failed: Soil chemistry parameters were fixed, creating fundamental supply limitation that no amount of plant-side optimization can overcome
alternatives: Two-stage calibration (soil chemistry then plant traits)
Include soil parameters in ensemble sampling

failed_approaches.approach: Increasing plant P uptake capacity (vmax_p) by 10× to overcome P limitation
failed_approaches.why_failed: Soil can't supply P fast enough due to slow desorption rate - like trying to cure thirst by making someone more thirsty when water supply is the problem

failed_approaches.approach: Aggressive parameter removal using never in top 20 across ANY output, average rank > 100 criteria
failed_approaches.why_failed: User feedback indicated most flagged parameters appear important through edge analyses, and cross-PFT principle should be applied
alternatives: Keep all parameters and add missing ones

failed_approaches.approach: Remove parameters that appear consistently low sensitivity across outputs
failed_approaches.why_failed: Cross-PFT effects are pervasive, edge parameters may appear insensitive but are constrained, and context-dependent effects not captured by mean biomass analysis
alternatives: Group parameters by base name using cross-PFT principle
Apply much more conservative removal criteria

failed_approaches.approach: Wide exploratory bounds [0.1, 30.0] for root distribution parameters
failed_approaches.why_failed: User questioned why not use small changes around calibrated parameters instead of arbitrary wide ranges

failed_approaches.approach: PFT-specific parameter expansion (expanding only PFT#10 parameters)
failed_approaches.why_failed: User pointed out it's unfair to expand parameters for one PFT but not others - lacks scientific consistency
alternatives: Uniform expansion across all 3 Arctic PFTs

failed_approaches.approach: Initial hypothesis that higher r_desorp would improve P availability
failed_approaches.why_failed: Higher r_desorp actually caused ecosystem collapse by creating conditions that led to drought-induced vegetation death and P trapping in litter
alternatives: Modify PID controller response during drought

failed_approaches.approach: Enable SUPLPHOS=ALL or SUPLNITRO=ALL during TRANSIENT phase
failed_approaches.why_failed: Transient runs represent real ecosystem conditions. Enabling nutrient supplementation during TRANS is equivalent to a fertilization experiment, not calibration. P/N supply problems must be fixed via spinup protocol (ADSP/RGSP supplementation), parameter tuning (uptake kinetics, stoichiometry, retranslocation), or soil initial conditions.
alternatives: Enable SUPLPHOS during ADSP/RGSP spinup phases only
Tune P uptake kinetics (vmax_p, km_p, vmax_ptase)
Extend spinup duration for better P cycling equilibrium
